batch: System Protection enabled-volume state API source review

sources.title: Enable-ComputerRestore
sources.finding: The cmdlet documentation explicitly directs operators to Rstrui.exe to find System Restore state for each drive. It also documents system-drive enablement dependency and client-only support.

sources.title: SystemRestore WMI class
sources.finding: Documented properties are restore-point metadata (description, type, sequence and creation time); methods include Enable/Disable and restore-point actions. It does not document a per-volume protection-enabled property.

sources.title: SystemRestoreConfig WMI class
sources.finding: Its documented read-only fields cover scheduled checkpoint intervals, restore-point lifetime and maximum disk allocation percentage, not whether protection is enabled on a volume.

sources.title: Configuring System Restore
sources.finding: Microsoft describes SystemRestore and SystemRestoreConfig as separate WMI classes for control/restore-point actions and schedule/storage configuration.

conclusion: The reviewed official scripting/WMI references do not establish a reliable read-only per-volume enabled-state API. Use the native System Protection interface for operator inspection; do not infer protection from restore-point presence, disk allocation, or a generic shadow-copy inventory. Keep the RIDE automation candidate pending until an accepted, stable read-only status source and current-build behavior are proven.

resolved: Documented the current source boundary for automated System Protection state inspection.
partial: The accepted Windows 11 On/advanced-Off design still lacks a proven scriptable status/readback route, affected-volume capture and async completion evidence.
deferred: Automated System Protection operation implementation and Windows 11 acceptance pending reliable per-volume observation and recovery semantics.

estimates.adjustment: None; source review closes no legacy setting outcome.
